name: Letter physics
look: A bold claim stands readable on the inverse ground, breathes in and flies apart in 3D in one short burst: every letter leaves along its own line from the centre with spin and a little gravity, the middle letters rushing nearest the viewer, each gone before the screen's edge cuts it. While the last letters leave, the one-sentence answer is already coming out of depth, whole, and lands at the claim's size on the page's own ground; a photograph behind it comes up like a room's lights, dimmed to the ground under the words.
reduced: The claim with the answer under it on the inverse ground, the photograph faint at the edges.
phone: The light version: the letters fade and drift instead of flying in depth.

needs.words: a claim of 12-36 characters and an answer of 16-60 characters that answers it
needs.photo: optional: one dark photograph with a calm centre

never: a glow or blurred type under the answer; a claim over 40 characters; on a calm or clinical brief (the burst reads as loud); on a product page about a physical thing
